content.title: About
content.content: Cashews are the kidney-shaped seeds of the cashew tree (Anacardium occidentale), native to northeastern Brazil and now grown in tropical regions around the world. The nut hangs below a fleshy cashew apple and has a creamy, buttery, mildly sweet flavor. Cashews are eaten as a snack and used in stir-fries, curries, sauces, desserts, and plant-based dairy alternatives.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The cashew nut grows outside the cashew apple, a fruit that is also edible but highly perishable.
Cashews are related to mangoes, pistachios, and poison ivy.
The shell contains a caustic oil that can irritate skin, so cashews are always sold shelled and processed.
Cashews are used to make creamy plant-based sauces, cheeses, and milks.
Major cashew producers include Vietnam, India, and countries in West Africa.

items.title: Provides healthy fats
items.content: Cashews contain mostly unsaturated fats, which can be part of a heart-friendly diet.

items.title: Provides magnesium and copper
items.content: These minerals support muscle, nerve, and metabolic function.

items.title: Provides zinc and manganese
items.content: These support immune function and normal metabolism.

items.title: Provides protein
items.content: Cashews provide plant protein, which supports fullness.

items.title: Contains vitamin K and antioxidants
items.content: Cashews provide vitamin K and plant compounds with antioxidant properties.

items.title: Tree nut allergy
items.content: Cashew allergy is among the more common tree nut allergies and can be severe. People allergic to cashews may also react to pistachios.

items.title: High in calories
items.content: Cashews are calorie-dense, so portions should be moderate.

items.title: Added salt
items.content: Roasted and salted cashews can contain a lot of sodium.

items.title: Oxalates
items.content: Cashews contain oxalates, which people prone to kidney stones may need to limit.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Cashews can be eaten as a snack, added to stir-fries, curries, salads, granola, and baked goods, or blended into creamy sauces, dips, desserts, and plant-based milks. Soaking cashews softens them for blending. Choose unsalted cashews when possible.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store cashews in an airtight container in a cool, dry, dark place, or in the refrigerator or freezer for longer storage, since their oils can turn rancid. Discard cashews that smell sharp or taste bitter.

content.title: About
content.content: The Chicken Fillet Sandwich (NFS 1773) is a ready‑to‑eat sandwich consisting of tender chicken fillet, fresh vegetables, a yogurt‑based sauce and a soft whole‑grain bun. It is designed for quick meals at the office, school or on the go.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The sandwich is part of the NFS line – products created for convenient nutrition without cooking.
The chicken fillet is thermally processed at a minimum of 75 °C, ensuring safety.
The bun is made from whole‑grain flour, increasing dietary fiber content.
The sauce is yogurt‑based, lowering calories compared with traditional mayonnaise sauces.
The product has a shelf life of 12 months when stored in a cool, dry place.

items.title: High in protein
items.content: Chicken fillet provides high‑quality protein essential for muscle growth and repair.

items.title: Low in saturated fat
items.content: Compared with typical sandwiches, this product contains less saturated fat, supporting cardiovascular health.

items.title: Source of B‑vitamins
items.content: Chicken meat and whole‑grain bun supply vitamins B6 and B12, important for metabolism.

items.title: Dietary fiber
items.content: The whole‑grain bun adds fiber, aiding normal digestion.

items.title: Low sugar content
items.content: No added sugars make this sandwich suitable for blood‑glucose management.

items.title: Chicken allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to chicken proteins.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Salt used in the sauce and marination can increase overall sodium intake.

items.title: Storage requirements
items.content: Improper storage (moisture, high temperature) may cause spoilage.

items.title: Preservatives
items.content: The product may contain food preservatives that can affect sensitive consumers.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: The sandwich is ready to eat straight from the package. If desired, heat in a microwave for 30‑40 seconds to soften the bun and warm the fillet.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store in a dry, cool place at 10 °C–25 °C. After opening, consume within 3‑5 days.

content.title: About
content.content: A chicken wing that is fried and coated with a crispy breading is a staple item in fast‑food restaurants. The wings are deep‑fried until golden brown, keeping the meat juicy while delivering a crunchy exterior.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Wings are commonly served with a variety of sauces: barbecue, hot, honey‑mustard, and more.
In the United States, wing consumption surged after the invention of Buffalo wings in 1964.
The coating often contains a blend of flour, spices, and breadcrumbs, giving the wings their distinctive flavor and texture.
Wings are a popular item in eating‑contests, with records measured by the number of wings consumed in a set time.
In some regions, wings are accompanied by carrot and celery sticks to balance the richness.

items.title: Source of protein
items.content: Chicken wings provide high‑quality animal protein essential for muscle growth and tissue repair.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: The meat contains vitamins B6 and B12, which support nervous system function and metabolism.

items.title: Minerals
items.content: Wings supply iron, zinc, and phosphorus, important for immunity and bone health.

items.title: Satiety
items.content: The combination of protein and fat helps promote a feeling of fullness.

items.title: Energy boost
items.content: Wings provide a quick source of calories, convenient for fast‑food meals.

items.title: High fat and calorie content
items.content: Deep‑frying makes wings calorie‑dense and high in saturated fats, which can contribute to weight gain if eaten frequently.

items.title: Salt and sauces
items.content: Large amounts of salt and sugary or creamy sauces increase sodium intake and may affect blood pressure.

items.title: Chicken allergy
items.content: A small number of people may experience allergic reactions to chicken proteins.

items.title: Acrylamide formation
items.content: Cooking at very high temperatures can produce acrylamides, compounds that may be harmful in large amounts.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Wings are typically served hot and eaten with the hands, pulling the meat off the bone. They are often accompanied by dipping sauces, carrot and celery sticks, and french fries.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Cooked wings should be stored in the refrigerator for up to 2‑3 days in an airtight container. They can be frozen for up to 2 months and reheated in an oven or microwave before serving.

cookie-marshmallow-with-rice-cereal-no-b.title: No‑Bake Cookie with Marshmallow and Rice Cereal

content.title: About
content.content: This soft, no‑bake cookie is made from rolled oats, rice cereal, butter, sugar, marshmallows and a hint of vanilla. The mixture is shaped into small rounds and chilled until firm.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: No‑bake desserts retain more vitamins and minerals because they are not exposed to high heat.
Marshmallows add sweetness and a melt‑in‑your‑mouth texture, while rice cereal contributes a light crunch.
These treats are popular in the United States during summer when people prefer not to heat the oven.
The combination of oats and rice provides both complex carbs and quick‑release energy.

items.title: Source of dietary fiber
items.content: Oats and rice cereal are rich in fiber, which supports healthy digestion.

items.title: Contains healthy fats
items.content: Butter (or optional nuts) supplies monounsaturated fats that are heart‑friendly.

items.title: Quick energy boost
items.content: Sugar and marshmallows raise blood glucose rapidly, making the cookie a convenient pre‑workout snack.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Oats provide thiamine, niacin and folate, which aid metabolism.

items.title: Minerals
items.content: Rice cereal and butter contribute magnesium, phosphorus and iron.

items.title: High sugar content
items.content: The large amount of sugar and marshmallows can contribute to weight gain and increase the risk of cavities.

items.title: Dairy allergy
items.content: Butter makes the product unsuitable for those with lactose intolerance or milk allergy.

items.title: Gluten sensitivity
items.content: Rolled oats may contain gluten; gluten‑free oats should be used for people with celiac disease.

items.title: Choking hazard for children
items.content: Marshmallows and larger pieces can pose a choking risk for young kids.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Enjoy the cookie as a standalone snack, crumble it over yogurt or ice cream, or use it as a base for dessert parfaits. Keep it chilled to maintain its shape.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 7 days. For longer keeping, freeze in a freezer‑safe bag, noting that texture may change slightly.

content.title: About
content.content: Fruit punch is a refreshing alcoholic beverage made from a blend of fruit juices, sugar, and spirits (usually vodka or rum). It has a bright fruit aroma, a sweet‑tart taste, and a moderate alcohol strength, typically 10–15% ABV.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Historically, punch was created in colonial regions using local fruits and sugar syrup.
There are countless variations: berry, tropical, citrus, or spiced with exotic herbs.
In some countries punch is served at “punch bars,” where guests can customize their drink.
Alcoholic punch is often used as a base for cocktails and dessert sauces.

items.title: Vitamins and Antioxidants
items.content: The fruit juices in punch provide vitamin C and other antioxidants that support the immune system.

items.title: Mood Enhancement
items.content: Moderate alcohol consumption can promote relaxation and improve mood.

items.title: Hydration
items.content: The water content of the juices helps maintain hydration, especially in warm weather.

items.title: Alcohol
items.content: Excessive intake can lead to intoxication, liver damage, and other health issues.

items.title: Sugar
items.content: High sugar levels increase the risk of cavities, weight gain, and blood‑glucose spikes.

items.title: Allergy to Ingredients
items.content: Some fruit juices may trigger allergic reactions in sensitive individuals.

content.title: How to Drink
content.content: Serve the punch chilled in glasses or tumblers over ice. Garnish with fruit slices, mint, or berries. For a lighter version, top with sparkling water.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the prepared punch in a sealed bottle in the refrigerator for up to 5 days. Store individual ingredients (juice, spirit) in a cool, dark place for longer shelf life.

content.title: About
content.content: The Light Ice Cream Sandwich is made of two delicate wafer cookies filled with a layer of chocolate ice cream. The product has lower calories than traditional ice cream sandwiches thanks to a light cream base and reduced sugar content.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The first chocolate ice cream sandwich appeared in the United States in the 1970s.
The light version was developed in the 2010s to cut calories without sacrificing taste.
It uses natural cocoa powder instead of artificial flavorings.
Each sandwich is individually wrapped in an aluminum film to preserve freshness.
The product is often used in culinary workshops as a base for dessert decorations.

items.title: Low Calorie
items.content: The light formula provides about 150 kcal per serving, allowing it to fit into a balanced diet.

items.title: Source of Calcium
items.content: The dairy base supplies roughly 10 % of the daily calcium requirement, supporting bone health.

items.title: Contains Antioxidants
items.content: Cocoa powder is rich in flavonoids, which help combat free radicals.

items.title: Energy Support
items.content: A modest amount of carbohydrates offers a quick source of energy after workouts.

items.title: Reduced Sugar
items.content: Lower sugar levels make the product more suitable for those monitoring glycemic impact.

items.title: Milk Protein Allergy
items.content: The product contains milk and may trigger allergic reactions in sensitive individuals.

items.title: Gluten Content
items.content: The wafers contain wheat, so it is not suitable for a gluten‑free diet.

items.title: Storage at High Temperatures
items.content: Prolonged storage at room temperature can cause the ice cream to melt, affecting texture and flavor.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Keep the sandwich frozen and serve immediately after removal. It can be halved and topped with berries, nuts, or grated chocolate for extra flavor.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store in the freezer at –18 °C or lower. Once opened, consume within 2‑3 days and avoid refreezing.

content.title: About
content.content: Mashed potato with gravy is a popular side dish in fast‑food restaurants. It is made from boiled potatoes mashed to a creamy consistency, mixed with butter, milk, and a thick meat or vegetable gravy. Served hot in individual containers.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Mashed potatoes are often served as a standalone side, but in fast‑food they are frequently used as a base for chicken nuggets or burgers.
Gravy can be meat‑based (beef, chicken) or vegetable‑based (mushroom, tomato).
In the United States the average fast‑food mashed‑potato portion is about 200 g.
Mashed potatoes are one of the cheapest sides, which makes them a staple for chain restaurants.
There is a “loaded mash” version where finely diced vegetables are mixed in to boost nutrition.

items.title: Rich in potassium
items.content: Potatoes provide potassium, which supports normal blood pressure and muscle function.

items.title: Vitamin C source
items.content: Small amounts of vitamin C remain in the mash, offering antioxidant benefits.

items.title: Energy‑dense carbs
items.content: Starch delivers quick‑acting energy for the body.

items.title: Easy to digest
items.content: The smooth texture makes it suitable for children and people with chewing difficulties.

items.title: Contains dietary fiber
items.content: If the skin is left on, the mash adds fiber that aids digestion.

items.title: High sodium content
items.content: Gravy often contains a lot of salt, which can be problematic for hypertension.

items.title: Calorie density
items.content: Butter and milk make the mash calorie‑rich; portion control is advised.

items.title: Possible trans fats
items.content: Some fast‑food chains use partially hydrogenated oils in gravy, adding trans fats.

items.title: Dairy allergy
items.content: People with lactose intolerance or milk allergy should choose a dairy‑free version.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Mashed potato with gravy is served hot in a separate bowl. Eat with a spoon, pair with chicken nuggets, burgers, patties, or enjoy it as a standalone side.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store in the refrigerator in an airtight container for 2‑3 days. When reheating, add a splash of milk or water to restore creaminess. Do not leave at room temperature for more than 2 hours.
